title: Filtering the products table by numbers · part 39

steps.title: Keep stock >= 12
steps.prompt:
Numbers compare with small symbols:
  > bigger   < smaller   = exactly   != not equal
Keep the rows where stock is at least 12.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT id FROM products WHERE stock >= 12;
hints: Start with SELECT id FROM products.
Add WHERE after the table name.
The test is stock >= 12.
Write: SELECT id FROM products WHERE stock >= 12;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT id FROM products WHERE stock >= 12;
steps.memory_trick: WHERE keeps only the rows that pass the test.

steps.title: Count rows stock >= 12
steps.prompt: COUNT(*) counts how many rows survive the filter.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT count(*) FROM products WHERE stock >= 12;
hints: Start with SELECT count(*).
FROM products.
Add WHERE stock >= 12.
Write: SELECT count(*) FROM products WHERE stock >= 12;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM products WHERE stock >= 12;
steps.memory_trick: count(*) + WHERE = 'how many pass?'

steps.title: Filter then sort: stock >= 12
steps.prompt:
Filter first, then ORDER BY tidies what is left.
LIMIT 3 keeps the top of that sorted list.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT id FROM products WHERE stock >= 12 ORDER BY stock LIMIT 3;
hints: Start with SELECT id FROM products.
Add WHERE stock >= 12.
Add ORDER BY stock LIMIT 3.
Write: SELECT id FROM products WHERE stock >= 12 ORDER BY stock LIMIT 3;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT id FROM products WHERE stock >= 12 ORDER BY stock LIMIT 3;
steps.memory_trick: WHERE trims, ORDER BY sorts, LIMIT cuts.
